Matching SAS PROC MIXED

Source: vignettes/sas.Rmd
sas.Rmd

predictmeans aims to give the numbers SAS PROC MIXED gives for the same model. This page shows which arguments correspond to which SAS options, and what has been checked.

Options

SAS PROC MIXED predictmeans
METHOD=REML lmer(..., REML = TRUE), lme(), gls() (the defaults)
LSMEANS / DIFF CL predictmeans(): $means, $pairs
LSMEANS / OM weights = "proportional"
LSMEANS / ADJUST=TUKEY, SIMULATE adj = "tukey", "mvt"
ESTIMATE, CONTRAST contrastmeans(), pm_joint()
DDFM=CONTAIN df_method = "containment"
DDFM=BETWITHIN df_method = "between-within" (lmer, lme, gls)
DDFM=SATTERTHWAITE df_method = "Satterthwaite" (lmer, lme, gls)
DDFM=KR df_method = "KR-SAS" (lmer, lme, gls)
REPEATED / TYPE=UN SUBJECT= gls(..., correlation = corSymm(), weights = varIdent())
EMPIRICAL vcov = "HC0" (or "HC3", ~ cluster; lm/glm)

df_method = "Kenward-Roger" (the default for REML lmer fits) is Kenward–Roger as pbkrtest and emmeans compute it, with the expected information of the variance parameters; SAS uses the observed information. They agree in balanced designs. With missing data they can differ: for the split plot below with one whole plot missing, the Kenward–Roger df of a whole-plot comparison are 9.25 with "Kenward-Roger" and 8.35 with "KR-SAS" (and in SAS).

library(predictmeans)
Oats <- as.data.frame(nlme::Oats)
Oats$nitro <- factor(Oats$nitro)
oats_wp <- droplevels(subset(Oats, !(Block == "I" & Variety == "Golden Rain")))
fm <- lmer(yield ~ Variety * nitro + (1 | Block/Variety), data = oats_wp)
dfs <- sapply(c("containment", "between-within", "Satterthwaite", "Kenward-Roger", "KR-SAS"),
              function(m) predictmeans(fm, "Variety", df_method = m, plot = FALSE,
                                       prtnum = FALSE)$pairs$df)
rownames(dfs) <- c("Golden Rain - Marvellous", "Golden Rain - Victory", "Marvellous - Victory")
round(dfs, 2)
#>                          containment between-within Satterthwaite Kenward-Roger
#> Golden Rain - Marvellous           9              9          8.35          9.25
#> Golden Rain - Victory              9              9          8.35          9.25
#> Marvellous - Victory               9              9          8.10          9.01
#>                          KR-SAS
#> Golden Rain - Marvellous   8.35
#> Golden Rain - Victory      8.35
#> Marvellous - Victory       8.10

The SAS values for these pairs are, in the same order: containment 9, 9, 9; between-within 9, 9, 9; Satterthwaite 8.35, 8.35, 8.10 (as here); Kenward–Roger 8.35, 8.35, 8.10.

What was checked

The SAS program dev/sas/pm-reference.sas (in the package sources) fits four data sets — Yates’ oats split plot, the same with one sub-plot missing, with one whole plot missing, and a repeated-measures trial with an unstructured covariance — with the four DDFM methods: 16 PROC MIXED runs. Their output was compared with predictmeans value by value (dev/sas/compare-sas.R): every variance component, LS-mean, difference (estimate, SE, df, limits) and Type 3 F test with its df agrees with what SAS prints, to its last digit, except LS-mean SEs that differ by about 2e-5 (relative) where the two programs stop their REML iterations.
